subject: Realtime sessions hang under surge - urgent SLA risk
messages:
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@veridian.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: support@veridian.ai
Date: 2027-05-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: realtime session stalls during morning surge

Tessa —

We hit a repeatable problem this morning between 08:50–09:05 PT during our morning ingestion spike. Several of our user-facing streams (SSE + WS) abruptly stop emitting partial tokens for ~6–12s, then resume. This causes our UI to show “response stalled” and several retries were fired by the client. Latency and error rate spiked on the dashboards; we have screenshots and a short video.

We captured a pcap and the session logs for 4 sessions (attached). Our SREs saw a pattern where client side sent a keepalive and the server did not echo chunked frames for a few seconds. No disconnect, just a freeze.

This is hitting traffic during a key demo with a payer partner — can we get an engineer on this asap? Per our contract SLA, these interruptions are a high-severity issue.

Thanks,
Sanjay Patel
CTO, Veridian Health

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-05-18T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: realtime session stalls during morning surge — initial triage

Tessa / Ben —

I looked at the provided pcap and session logs for the 08:50 window. Quick findings:
- Multiple streaming connections show continuous TCP keepalives but a pause in token frames from the backend from 08:51:02 to 08:51:09.
- In the backend traces, we observe a short-lived spike in gRPC write latency on node gpu-8-3; the write loop for the model worker blocked for ~6.2s before flushing queued tokens.
- The worker logs include an out-of-memory (OOM) proxying event in the quantized execution path; it appears the kernel fallback triggered heavier memory operations and the VM reclaimed caches briefly.

I’ve attached a short dump and the raw pcap to this thread. I recommend the following immediate mitigations:
1) Route Veridian traffic to a different pool that has a different quantization profile (lower memory pressure). I can implement a targeted routing rule and roll it out in 15–20 minutes.
2) Increase our worker keepalive thresholds to avoid client-visible stalls while the worker recovers. This is a short-term stopgap.
3) Schedule a patch to the kernel fallback path to avoid synchronous cache reclamation under pressure (requires engineering time).

Given the OOM proxy hint, this looks like a load-pattern-triggered memory regression rather than a pure network timeout. I’ll open INFR-8271 and attach the trace.

-Aditya
Lead Inference Engineer, Redwood

1) We have a customer-facing demo scheduled Monday where a failed stream would be catastrophic for the deal. If you route us to a safer pool today we can validate.
2) Our contract has an SLA credit clause tied to >1% streaming failures per hour. We saw a ~2.4% failure spike for that 15-minute window. We’ll need confirmation of mitigation and timeframe to repair.

Also sharing a short screencast showing the UI behavior (link in Drive). Please advise next steps and ETA.

Sanjay

Subject: EXEC ESCALATION: Veridian — repeated streaming frame freezes during surge (need exec visibility)

Team —

Summary: Veridian Health experienced a reproducible streaming freeze during a morning throughput surge on 2027-05-18 (08:50 PT window). Root cause appears to be a memory-pressure-induced kernel fallback on the model worker (Aditya’s triage). Observable impact: intermittent client-visible stalls of 6–12s, ~2.4% failure spike for the 15-minute window, risk to an upcoming demo and SLA credit exposure.

Immediate actions taken:
- Re-routed Veridian traffic away from the affected worker pool at 10:30 PT on 2027-05-18 (Aditya).
- Opened INFR-8271 and attached traces.
- Customer notified and given hourly updates; Ben is coordinating post-mortem call and customer mitigation checklist.

Pending asks for leadership:
- Exec visibility: Please review INFR-8271 and concur on prioritized funding for a mid-cycle runtime patch (kernel fallback optimization). Estimated engineering effort 2–3 weeks.
- Contract posture: Marissa, can you confirm whether we should offer a one-time credit pending root-cause completion? Customer has already flagged demo risk.
- Customer communication: I propose a shared war-room with Veridian for Monday (link in related_links) — approval to schedule and staff is needed.

Attachments and artifacts: ws-trace-20270518-0900.pcap; veridian_session_0423_logs.zip; error-rate-graph-may2027.png. Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFR-8271.

I’ll be on standby and can join an exec sync if helpful.

Best,
